summary: Things that make tamei, when split into two halves, can they still join together to make a person tamei? Rabbi Dosa says no, and the Sages say yes, unless the two halves make him tamei in two different ways.

chunks.en: All things that make tamei in a tent which were split,
and he brought them into the house,
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says it is tahor,
and the Sages say it is tamei.
How is this? One who touches two halves of an olive's size

words.note: The size of half an olive.

chunks.en: of a neveilah, or carries them,

words.note: An animal that died without shechitah.

chunks.he: וּבַמֵּת, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכַחֲצִי זַיִת וּמַאֲהִיל עַל
chunks.en: and with a dead person: one who touches half an olive's size and is over
half an olive's size, or touches half
an olive's size and half an olive's size is over him,
or is over two halves of an olive's size,
is over half an olive's size
and half an olive's size is over him,
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas
says tahor and the Sages say tamei.

chunks.he: אֲבָל הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכַחֲצִי זַיִת וְדָבָר אַחֵר
chunks.en: But one who touches half an olive's size, and something else
is over him and over half an olive's size,

chunks.he: אוֹ מַאֲהִיל עַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וְדָבָר
chunks.en: or is over half an olive's size, and something

chunks.he: אַחֵר מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו וְעַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת,
chunks.en: else is over him and over half an olive's size,
is tahor. Rabbi Meir said:
even here Rabbi Dosa
says tahor and the Sages say tamei.
Everything is tamei,
except touching together with carrying,
and carrying together with a tent.
This is the rule:
whatever is from one name
chunks.explain: The same kind of tumah, like two touchings.

chunks.en: is tamei. From two names, it is tahor.

summary: Rabbi Dosa and the Sages argue about three things: whether pieces of food add up, whether maaser sheni can be switched onto a blank coin, and dipping hands for the parah adumah.

chunks.en: Food in separate pieces
does not add up,
the words of Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas.
And the Sages say:

chunks.he: מִצְטָרֵף. מְחַלְּלִין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי עַל אֲסִימוֹן,
chunks.en: it adds up. We may redeem maaser sheni onto a blank coin,

words.note: A metal coin with no picture stamped on it yet.

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
we may not redeem.
We may dip just the hands for the chatas water,
chunks.explain: The water mixed with ashes of the parah adumah.

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
if his hands became tamei,
his whole body became tamei.

summary: May a non-Kohen eat the inside of a terumah melon or the thrown-away leaves of terumah vegetables? And how much wool from five sheep must be given to the Kohen?

chunks.he: מְעֵי אֲבַטִּיחַ וּקְנִיבַת יָרָק שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
chunks.en: The inside of a melon and the trimmed leaves of a vegetable of terumah,
Rabbi Dosa allows them to non-Kohanim,
and the Sages forbid.

chunks.he: חָמֵשׁ רְחֵלוֹת גְּזוּזוֹת מָנֶה מָנֶה וּפְרַס,
chunks.en: Five sheep whose wool came to a maneh and a half each,
must give the first of the shearing,

words.note: Some wool that is given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
five sheep, any amount at all.

summary: Which mats and woven things can become tamei? Rabbi Dosa and the Sages argue.

chunks.en: All mats can become tamei from a dead body,
the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
from treading. All woven bands are tahor,

words.note: Tumah from a zav standing or sitting on it.

chunks.en: except those of a galgilon,

words.note: A kind of belt or band.

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
all of them can become tamei,
except those of wool workers.

summary: A sling for throwing stones: when can it become tamei, and when is it tahor?

chunks.en: A sling whose holder is woven,
can become tamei. And one of leather,
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas
says tahor and the Sages say tamei.
If its finger loop was torn off,
it is tahor. If its holding-strap was torn off, it is tamei.

summary: A woman who was taken captive: may she still eat terumah? It depends on whether we only know about it from her own words.

chunks.en: A woman who was taken captive may eat terumah,
the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say:
there is a captive woman who eats and there is
a captive woman who does not eat.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁאָמְרָה נִשְׁבֵּיתִי וּטְהוֹרָה אָנִי,
chunks.en: How? A woman who said, "I was captured, and I am tahor,"

chunks.he: אוֹכֶלֶת, שֶׁהַפֶּה שֶׁאָסַר הוּא הַפֶּה שֶׁהִתִּיר.
chunks.en: eats, because the mouth that forbade is the mouth that allowed.
chunks.explain: We only know she was captured from her own words.

chunks.en: And if there are witnesses that she was captured,
and she says, "I am tahor,"
she does not eat.

summary: In four cases of doubt about whether something touched tumah, Rabbi Yehoshua says it is tamei and the Sages say it is tahor.

chunks.en: Four doubts that Rabbi Yehoshua says are tamei,
and the Sages say are tahor.
How? The tamei one stands and the tahor one passes by,
the tahor one stands and the tamei one passes by,

chunks.he: טֻמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְטָהֳרָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: tumah in a private place and taharah in a public place,

chunks.he: טָהֳרָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְטֻמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: taharah in a private place and tumah in a public place,
maybe he touched, maybe he did not touch,
maybe he was over it, maybe he was not over it,
maybe he moved it, maybe he did not move it,
Rabbi Yehoshua says tamei,
and the Sages say tahor.

summary: Rabbi Tzadok says three metal or wooden things can become tamei, and the Sages say they cannot.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok says three things are tamei,
and the Sages say tahor:
the nail of a money changer,
and a chest of grist-makers,

words.note: People who grind beans and grain.

chunks.en: and the nail of a sundial stone,

words.note: A sundial that tells the time.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok says tamei and the Sages say tahor.

summary: Rabban Gamliel says four metal things can become tamei and the Sages say they cannot. The Sages agree about a tablet split into a big piece and a small piece.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says four things are tamei,
and the Sages say tahor:
a metal cover of a basket
of homeowners,
and the hook for scrapers,

words.note: Metal tools used to scrape the skin in the bathhouse.

chunks.en: and unfinished metal vessels,
and a tablet that was split in two.
And the Sages agree with Rabban Gamliel
about a tablet that was split in two,
one big and one small,
the big one is tamei and the small one is tahor.

summary: In three things about Yom Tov, Rabban Gamliel was strict like Beis Shammai. The Sages said his family could be strict on themselves but allowed it for all Yisrael.

chunks.en: In three things Rabban Gamliel
is strict like the words of Beis Shammai.
We do not wrap up hot food
from Yom Tov for Shabbos,

chunks.he: וְאֵין זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמְּנוֹרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: and we do not put together the menorah on Yom Tov,

chunks.he: וְאֵין אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין.
chunks.en: and we do not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.he: מִימֵיהֶן שֶׁל בֵּית אַבָּא לֹא הָיוּ
chunks.en: In all the days of my father's house they did not
bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
They said to him:

chunks.he: מַה נַּעֲשֶׂה לְבֵית אָבִיךָ שֶׁהָיוּ מַחְמִירִין
chunks.en: What can we do about your father's house, who were strict

chunks.he: עַל עַצְמָן וּמְקִלִּין עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת
chunks.en: on themselves and easy on Yisrael, letting them
bake thick loaves and white bread.

summary: Rabban Gamliel also allowed three things on Yom Tov: sweeping between the beds, putting spices on coals, and making a roasted goat on Pesach night. The Sages forbid them.

chunks.he: אַף הוּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים לְהָקֵל.
chunks.en: He also said three things to be easy.
We may sweep between the beds,
and put the spices on the coals on Yom Tov,

words.note: Sweet-smelling spices put on hot coals.

chunks.en: and make a whole roasted goat on Pesach night.
And the Sages forbid.

summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah allowed three things that the Sages forbid: his cow going out on Shabbos with a strap, combing an animal on Yom Tov, and grinding pepper in a pepper mill.

chunks.en: Three things that Rabbi Elazar
ben Azaryah allows,
and the Sages forbid.
His cow went out with a strap between her horns,
and we may comb an animal on Yom Tov,
and we may grind the peppers in their own mill.
Rabbi Yehudah says:

chunks.he: אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: we may not comb an animal on Yom Tov,
because it makes a wound,
but we may scrape it.
And the Sages say:
we may not comb, and we may not even scrape.
